The genealogies of Genesis go beyond simply recording history. By selective information and by structure, they communicate spiritual truth. The genealogies highlight God’s blessing, authenticate the family heritage of important individuals, and hold the Genesis narrative together by showing familial continuity. Adam’s genealogy through Seth traces ten generations to Noah (see
), with the flood intervening before another ten generations from Noah to Abram. The number ten indicates completeness (ten plagues,
). Noah closed history before the flood, and Abram inaugurated a new era.
